prompt:
A single compound was assayed by IC50 against a single protein target in two different assays, reported in the literature.

Compound SMILES: C[S+]([O-])c1ccc(-c2nc(-c3ccc(F)cc3)c(-c3ccncc3)[nH]2)cc1
Target (ChEMBL): CHEMBL260

Assay A:
  Description: Inhibition of p38a MAPK (unknown origin) by radiometric assay
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Homo sapiens

Assay B:
  Description: Inhibition of p38alpha MAPK (unknown origin) using ATF-2 as substrate after 1 hr by ELISA
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Homo sapiens

Will the two reported IC50 values agree closely (within 0.3 log units), or differ substantially (more than 1.0 log units)?

Respond with exactly this JSON and nothing else:
{"call": "COMMENSURABLE" | "NOT_COMMENSURABLE" | "INSUFFICIENT_INFO",
 "confidence": <float 0-1>,
 "error_class": "assay_method" | "buffer_conditions" | "construct_mutant" | "organism" | "readout_type" | "potency_range" | "none" | "other",
 "reason": "<one sentence>"}

"COMMENSURABLE" means you expect the two reported values to agree closely.
"NOT_COMMENSURABLE" means you expect them to differ substantially.
error_class is your primary reason for a NOT_COMMENSURABLE call, else "none".
raw: {"call": "COMMENSURABLE", "confidence": 0.6, "error_class": "none", "reason": "Both assays measure IC50 for inhibition of human p38α MAPK with high confidence scores, and although the detection methods differ (radiometric vs. ELISA with ATF-2 substrate), they are both functional kinase inhibition assays targeting the same enzyme, so IC50 values are expected to agree within ~0.3 log units for a potent, well-behaved inhibitor."}
